liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Reviewer loves this version; the first set was tight [11]
- **West LA Fadeaway** (1 review): Second set was hot, with West L.A. Fadeaway singled out as a highlight [9]
- **Masterpiece** (1 review): Reviewer calls Masterpiece good; says the show improves as it goes on [15]

## Setlist highlights

- **Baba O'Riley**: rare: 12 archived performances [20]
- **Tomorrow Never Knows**: rare: 12 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1992-07-01.140226.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 144 min [1]
- **gd92-07-01.prefm.ladner.5701.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 20 songs; 144 min; rated 3.07/5 by 44 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the sound quality phenomenal, with keyboards prominent in the mix; Reviewer finds this recording sounds pretty nice; Reviewer calls the recording perfect [9][10][11][14]
- **gd1992-07-01.fob.schoeps.evans.gems.81844.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 144 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [6]
- **gd1992-07-01.147571.beyerCM101.ebel.flac1648**: source not stated; 20 songs; 150 min [7]

## Around the show

- Guest harmonica player joined for really strong jamming; Jerry's voice sounded somewhat frayed [9]
- Attendee describes crushing crowd at the front during the opener Steve Miller, heat, and a naked, stoned woman escorted off via the stage [10]
- Huge crowd in an open field, typical of Buckeye Lake shows; attendee remembers the show feeling longer than the download [11]
- Attendee says this closed the Midwest and East Coast summer tour, and no flute player appeared in set one [12]
- Doubts the earlier claim of a flute player; finds the second set flat and dislikes the setlist [13]
- Left before set one ended; says Jerry looked tired, band seemed worn at tour's end, and beer was expensive inside [14]
- Attendee stood near the soundboard and denies any flute in set one, suggesting Jerry's MIDI instead [16]
- Long entry lines, a big balloon knocked the reviewer down, and a friend briefly played harmonica in the crowd during set one [17]
- Second set was not the longest ever, but the first set was incredibly tight [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1992-07-01.140226.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Tascam Deck/TDK SA-X100) [1]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to make the show complete; this file set is 16 bit [1]
- **gd92-07-01.prefm.ladner.5701.sbeok.shnf**: source: preFM SBD > CM > DAT > CDR > WAV > SHNv3 [3]
- **gd1992-07-01.fob.schoeps.evans.gems.81844.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Todd Evans; transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: Schoeps CMC32's (8 foot spaced omnis on 6 foot stands) -> Monster M1000 Cable -> Oade Mic Preamp -> Monster M1000 Jumper Cables -> Panasonic sv255 DAT Deck [6]. Also: DAT from Todd Evans collection, played through a TASCAM DA-20 and M-Audio FireWire Solo into Soundforge 8.0; transferred March 14, 2006 [6]
- **gd1992-07-01.147571.beyerCM101.ebel.flac1648**: taped by Pete Ebel; transferred by Transfers by Pete Ebel March 31, 2018; source: Beyer CM 101-> Casio DA-7-> DAT (Taped by Pete Ebel) [7]. Also: Transferred from DAT to wav at 48k; the first 25 seconds of Midnight Hour come from another source because of a tape cut [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Sameh Tawfik Grateful Dead: [1992-07-01 Buckeye Lake Music Center, Hebron, OH, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1992-07-01-buckeye-lake-music-center-hebron-oh-usa/) [21]
- Fan art by Sameh Tawfik Grateful Dead: [1992-07-01 Buckeye Lake Music Center, Hebron, OH, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1992-07-01-buckeye-lake-music-center-hebron-oh-usa/) [22]
- Poster by Sameh Tawfik Grateful Dead: [1992-07-01 Buckeye Lake Music Center, Hebron, OH, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1992-07-01-buckeye-lake-music-center-hebron-oh-usa/) [23]
